title: A Primitive's Global Activation Status and each instance's Status are independent lifecycles
content:
A.2.2.1.3.1 establishes a two-level state model. Each valid Invocation updates the Agent Artifact with a specific *instance* of a Primitive — "each Invocation of the Token SkyLink Primitive launches a SkyLink deployment to a specific blockchain" — and "A Primitive instance thus has its own Status or life cycle that is independent of the Primitive's Global Activation Status."

Instance Status is a strict three-value enum, and A.2.2.1.3.2 requires exactly one at all times: `Active` (fully operational for its intended purpose), `Suspended` (was Active, may be again — cited causes include underperformance, security issues, or breaching Risk Capital or Asset Liability Management requirements), and `Completed` (terminal, either permanently ceased or a single-Invocation deployment that has achieved its outcome, such as the Prime Transformation Primitive).

The separation is what makes Primitives operationally usable. A.2.2.1.3.3 shows the payoff: an Agent "may run multiple Integration Boost instances in parallel (each with its own markets and configurations), toggling them on or off as needed, without affecting the underlying Integration Boost Primitive's Global Activation Status." Global status is a *permission*; instance status is *operations*.

The two levels also carry different governance weights. Global status changes post-launch require a token holder vote plus Operational Executor Facilitator review (A.2.2.1.2.4.1.3), while instance changes can run through Root Edit governance or an appropriately configured Omni Document (A.2.2.1.3.3). Day-to-day operational agility is deliberately cheaper than changing what the Agent is permitted to do at all.
description: One activated Primitive can back many instances — parallel Integration Boost configurations, per-chain SkyLink deployments — each suspended or resumed without touching global status.
